headline: Hackers are actively exploiting an unauthenticated macOS Screen Sharing flaw to seize full control of Macs and mine Monero, while AI reshapes vulnerability triage, content watermarking, and agent identity across the industry.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep turning public proof-of-concept code into live intrusions within days, and the macOS Screen Sharing authentication bypass moved from disclosure to Monero-mining campaigns almost immediately.
emerging_trends.topic_title: macOS Screen Sharing Flaw Under Active Attack

emerging_trends.text: AI-augmented research and scanning are pushing vulnerability disclosures to record volumes, leaving NIST to weigh whether AI itself can dig the resulting backlog out.
emerging_trends.topic_title: NIST Weighs AI to Tame Vulnerability Surge

emerging_trends.text: Vendors are racing to govern autonomous AI agents, and Cyera's billion-dollar purchase of Oasis Security bets that data and identity control must fuse into one plane before agent access proliferates.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Cyera Buys Oasis Security for Agent Control

topics.title: macOS Screen Sharing Flaw Under Active Attack
topics.latest_developments: Hackers began exploiting an unauthenticated macOS Screen Sharing bug to log in remotely without a password after public exploit code appeared, and the Netherlands' National Cyber Security Centre warns they are dropping a Monero cryptominer on compromised Macs.
topics.summary: The authentication-bypass flaw hands remote attackers full control of a Mac; Apple users should apply the latest macOS update and disable Screen Sharing where they do not need it.

sources.title: Vulnerability giving attackers full control of Macs is under active exploitation
Hackers exploit macOS Screen Sharing flaw to deploy Monero miner

topics.title: NIST Weighs AI to Tame Vulnerability Surge
topics.latest_developments: The National Institute of Standards and Technology is studying whether AI can help it triage a swelling backlog of vulnerabilities, as AI-augmented research and scanning drive disclosure volumes to new highs.
topics.summary: AI tools now surface software flaws faster than analysts can catalog them, straining the National Vulnerability Database; NIST is evaluating AI-assisted triage to keep pace.

sources.title: Amid AI-Driven Bug-Hunt Tsunami, NIST Looks to … AI

topics.title: Cyera Buys Oasis Security for Agent Control
topics.latest_developments: Cyera agreed to buy Oasis Security for roughly $1 billion, converging data security and identity into a single control plane that redefines privileged access for AI agents around business context instead of static roles.
topics.summary: The deal targets the governance gap that opens as autonomous AI agents gain reach into corporate data, folding Oasis's identity controls into Cyera's data-security platform.

sources.title: Cyera's Oasis Security Buy Is All About AI Agent Control

topics.title: Anthropic Builds Watermarks for Claude Text
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic detailed a plan to watermark the text that Claude generates, aiming to make AI-authored content easier to spot.
topics.summary: Watermarking would embed detectable signals in Claude's output so readers can distinguish machine-written text; Anthropic laid out how the technique would function.

sources.title: How Anthropic plans to watermark Claude's AI-generated text

topics.title: Scotland Crown Office Breach May Widen
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading reports the breach at Scotland's Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service may be widening, because the third-party supplier behind it possibly serviced other Scottish government agencies.
topics.summary: Intruders reached the prosecutor's office through a shared vendor, and investigators now fear the same supplier exposed additional agencies, enlarging the potential victim pool.

sources.title: Scottish Govt Suffers Potentially Widening Data Breach at Prosecutor's Office

weather: Tonight: Mostly Cloudy then Slight Chance Showers And Thunderstorms, low 70F.

business_politics.title: Trump Family Crypto Venture Wins Bank-Charter Approval
business_politics.latest_developments: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted World Liberty Financial preliminary conditional approval on August 14 to operate as a national trust bank.
business_politics.summary: World Liberty Financial, the flagship crypto venture tied to President Trump's family, cleared its first federal hurdle toward a bank charter, sharpening conflict-of-interest questions around the president's business holdings while he sits in office.

sources.title: US regulator grants banking licence to Trump family crypto venture
Trump Family's World Liberty Financial Gets Preliminary Approval to Launch a Bank

business_politics.title: Nvidia Pares Back OpenAI Data-Center Guarantee
business_politics.latest_developments: The Wall Street Journal reported August 14 that Nvidia is shrinking its planned $250 billion guarantee backing an OpenAI data center as investors question its risk exposure.
business_politics.summary: Nvidia has wielded its balance sheet to underwrite demand for its own AI chips, and trimming the OpenAI backstop signals unease over how much buildout risk the chipmaker can carry as Wall Street and private-credit lenders finance the AI boom.

sources.title: Nvidia Downsizes Plans for $250 Billion Guarantee of OpenAI Data Center

business.title: Little Italy Days Squeezes Bloomfield Eateries
business.latest_developments: KDKA reported August 15 that some Bloomfield restaurants take in less money during the annual Little Italy Days festival even as it draws tens of thousands to the neighborhood.
business.summary: Tessaro's owner David Vrenna and other Bloomfield business owners told KDKA the Liberty Avenue festival brings crowds and exposure but cuts into their usual sales, pushing some to sell food from tables out front and others to skip the event.

sources.title: Some Bloomfield eateries say Little Italy Days bring more exposure but less business
Some Bloomfield restaurants sell food out front during Little Italy Days

business.title: Station Square's Long Slide
business.latest_developments: Post-Gazette senior food writer Hal B. Klein set out on August 14 to explain why Station Square has faltered for years.
business.summary: Station Square, the South Shore retail, dining, and entertainment complex along the Monongahela River, has struggled for several years despite its prime waterfront location, and Post-Gazette dining critic Hal B. Klein examined what went wrong.

sources.title: Talk the Talk: Aug. 14, 2026

around_town.title: Garrity Lines Up to Challenge Shapiro for Governor
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette profiled on August 15 state Treasurer Stacy Garrity's Trump-backed bid to unseat Governor Josh Shapiro in 2026.
around_town.summary: Stacy Garrity, Pennsylvania's Republican state treasurer and a Trump endorsee, is mounting an ambitious, experienced campaign to deny Democratic Governor Josh Shapiro a second term, a race that tests whether the president's backing can overcome Shapiro's popularity.

sources.title: Stacy Garrity is ambitious, Trump-endorsed and experienced. Is that enough to beat Josh Shapiro?

around_town.title: Region's School Taxes Rise Across the Board
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported August 15 that most property owners across the region will pay higher school taxes in 2026-27.
around_town.summary: Facing inflation and rising costs, a majority of school districts in Western Pennsylvania raised property tax rates for the 2026-27 year, adding to homeowners' bills as classes resume.

sources.title: School districts fight inflation, rising costs as tax rates go up

around_town.title: Petition Targets Springdale Police Chief's Contract
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported August 15 that an online petition to end Springdale Police Chief Derek Dayoub's contract gathered about 250 signatures.
around_town.summary: Roughly 250 people have signed an online petition urging Springdale borough, in Allegheny County's Alle-Kiski Valley, to terminate the contract of Police Chief Derek Dayoub.

sources.title: Petition with hundreds of signatures calls for end to Springdale police chief's contract

around_teams.title: Steelers Extend Keeanu Benton
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported August 14 that the Steelers signed defensive tackle Keeanu Benton to a new deal it put at five years and $73.75 million, making him the highest-paid defensive lineman in franchise history.
around_teams.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers locked up third-year defensive tackle Keeanu Benton, the Wisconsin product, at roughly $18 million a year per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, committing to an interior anchor before the regular season opens.

sources.title: Steelers agree on a new 5-year, $73.75 million deal with Keeanu Benton

around_teams.title: Steelers Bring Back Elandon Roberts
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported that the Steelers are set to re-sign veteran linebacker Elandon Roberts.
around_teams.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are bringing back linebacker Elandon Roberts, adding an experienced hand to the front seven as roster decisions firm up ahead of the 2026 season.

sources.title: Source: The Steelers are set to bring back Elandon Roberts

around_teams.title: Hiles Says Shut Skenes Down If He Struggles
around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles argued August 15 that if ace Paul Skenes struggles again in Sunday's start, it should be his last outing of the season.
around_teams.summary: With the Pirates fading from contention, Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles wrote that the club should consider shutting down ace Paul Skenes to protect him, making Sunday's start potentially his final one of 2026 if it goes poorly.

sources.title: Noah Hiles: If Paul Skenes struggles again Sunday, it should be his last start of the season

team_usa.title: Pallister Beats Ledecky at Pan Pacs
team_usa.latest_developments: Australia's Lani Pallister beat American Katie Ledecky in the 400-meter freestyle at the Pan Pacific Championships on Friday, August 14.
team_usa.summary: Lani Pallister edged Katie Ledecky in the 400 free at the Pan Pacific Championships, a rare defeat for the American distance great, who opened the meet earlier in the week winning the 1,500 free as the United States set a world record in the 4x100 mixed medley relay.

sources.title: Pallister defeats Ledecky to win Pan Pacs 400 free
Ledecky wins, U.S. sets record to open Pan Pacs

team_usa.title: 1996 US Women's Hoops Team Enters Hall of Fame
team_usa.latest_developments: The Guardian reported August 15 that the 1996 United States women's Olympic basketball team enters the Hall of Fame on Saturday.
team_usa.summary: The 1996 US women's Olympic basketball team, whose home-soil gold in Atlanta gave momentum to the launch of the WNBA and reestablished American dominance after a 1992 semifinal loss, will be inducted into the Hall of Fame this weekend.

sources.title: 'Here we are 30 years later': the Olympic team that transformed US basketball

team_usa.title: Meyers Taylor Sits Out Bobsled World Cup Season
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported August 12 that Olympic monobob champion Elana Meyers Taylor will miss the coming World Cup bobsled season with post-concussion symptoms.
team_usa.summary: Elana Meyers Taylor, the United States monobob Olympic gold medalist, said months of post-concussion symptoms will keep her out of the entire upcoming World Cup bobsled season.

sources.title: Meyers Taylor to miss World Cup bobsled season

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: Premium: How Much Money Does AI Need?
reading.summary: Zitron tallies the enormous capital the AI industry keeps consuming and argues the sums required to sustain it are far larger and less justifiable than boosters admit.

reading.title: Anthropic's Watermarking, How It (Probably) Works, Worse Than It Seems
reading.summary: Ben Thompson argues Anthropic's move to watermark AI output in response to the EU's AI law is a bad idea, first on philosophical grounds and second because the mechanism likely works worse than it appears.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: On AI Coding and Its Discontents
reading.summary: Drawing on a converted skeptic engineer's account, Newport weighs what AI coding tools actually change about software work and the discontents that come with them.
